name: The Heavens
lines: the Greek gods, on the cloud-wrapped summit above the world
Homer's Olympos: the bronze-floored halls Hephaistos built for each god on the peak, above the clouds, where it is never shaken by wind nor wet with rain (Odyssey 6).
The Heavenly Capitol
the gods of Rome, on their marble hill
The Romans kept their great gods on the Capitol and their Pantheon to all of them; here their temples stand round a forum of white marble under the laurels.
the Æsir and Vanir, over Bifröst, under the World Tree
The Prose Edda: Asgard, reached over Bifröst, the burning rainbow bridge; each god has a hall of their own (Valhalla, Bilskirnir, Breiðablik, Fensalir), and the ash Yggdrasil stands over all.
The Field of Reeds
Aaru, the gods of the Two Lands, by the heavenly Nile
In the Book of the Dead the blessed dead go to Aaru, the Field of Reeds, a perfect Egypt of canals and fields; the gods' houses have pylon gates, obelisks and avenues of sphinxes.
Dilmun, the Pure Land
the gods of Sumer, Akkad and Babylon, by the sweet waters

In the Sumerian poem of Enki and Ninhursag, Dilmun is the pure, clean and bright land where the raven does not cry, the lion does not kill, and no one grows old; the sun god Utu brought it sweet water from the earth. The gods' houses stand on stepped platforms of mud brick among date palms, reeds and springs. (Babylon itself, the city of men, stands among the Wonders of the World.)
Garōdmān, the powers of the Persian light
Zoroastrian Garōdmān, the House of Song, is the highest heaven of light; the Persian garden (paradeisos, the root of 'paradise') is four streams round a pool, with cypresses and fire.
Svarga, on Mount Meru
the devas, round the golden mountain at the centre of the world
In the Puranas, Indra's Svarga stands on golden Mount Meru with the cities of the other gods round it; lotus pools, the wish-granting tree, and temple towers carved with a thousand figures.
the celestial bureaucracy and the immortals
The Jade Emperor rules heaven as a court with its ministries; the immortals keep the Peach Garden and the Kunlun mountains, where cranes fly and the gates are lacquer red.
the kami, on the High Plain of Heaven
The Kojiki's Takamagahara, the High Plain of Heaven, where Amaterasu rules; reached by the Floating Bridge of Heaven, with rice fields, a heavenly river and shrines behind their torii.
the Tuatha Dé Danann, in the Land of the Young
The Irish otherworld over the western sea: Tír na nÓg, Mag Mell, where no one grows old, with apple trees always in fruit and the sídhe under the green hills.
the old powers of the Welsh tales
Annwn, the Welsh otherworld of the Mabinogi, a land of plenty with the cauldron that never fails, ruled by Arawn and reached by lake and by mist.
the gods of Gaul, in the oak nemeton
The Gauls worshipped in the nemeton, a sacred grove of oaks (Lucan and Pliny wrote of it), with carved posts and the mistletoe the druids cut with a golden sickle.
the old gods of the forest and the hearth
Iriy (Vyraj), the Slavic otherworld where the birds fly for winter, at the top of the world oak; Perun's oak on the hill, the birches, and carved wooden halls.
the orisha, in the compound of heaven
For the Yoruba, Ọ̀run is the realm of Olódùmarè and the orisha; Osun's sacred grove at Osogbo with its river, carved posts and shrines under the palms is its likeness on earth.
Nyame, and the stories the spider bought
Nyame, the Akan sky god, kept all the stories until Kwaku Ananse bought them; Asante shrines were whitewashed and carved, and the Golden Stool came down from the sky.
the lwa, beneath the waters and at the crossroads
In Vodou the lwa dwell in Ginen, 'under the water', and come through the poto mitan, the centre post of the peristyle; vèvè are drawn on the ground to call them.
the gods of the Fifth Sun, on their pyramid temples
Omeyocan, the thirteenth heaven of the Mexica, and Tlalocan, Tlaloc's paradise of rain; their temples stood on stepped pyramids above canals and chinampa gardens of marigolds.
The Thirteen Heavens
the Maya gods, above the ceiba
The Maya world tree, the great ceiba, holds up thirteen layers of heaven; the Popol Vuh's hero twins rose to be the sun and the moon. Temples crown stepped pyramids in the forest.
Inti and the gods of the upper world
Hanan Pacha, the Inca upper world of Inti the sun and Mama Killa the moon; built in fitted stone on mountain terraces, with the golden sun disc of the Coricancha.
the gods of the islands and the long voyages
Hawaiki, the homeland the voyagers came from and the souls go back to; Pele's fire in Kīlauea, carved tiki at the heiau, and the open sea all round.
The Seventh Heaven
the hosts about the throne
Araboth, the seventh heaven of the later Jewish writings, where the hosts stand about the throne; light upon light, and gates of pearl.
The Shadowed Reach
those who were named elsewhere first, at the dark edge below the clouds

Named here because they were named elsewhere first: the grimoires' spirits, the shells of the tree, and those who refused, in every telling. They keep their halls on the dark rim where the clouds run out.
